sn52.1:1.2: Anuruddha was the brother of Ānanda and Mahānāma (Kd 17:1.1.3) which, according to the commentary, makes the Buddha his cousin. In this Saṁyutta he appears as an exponent of mindfulness meditation; he is well known also as a master of clairvoyance (AN 1.192:1.1). Many Suttas feature him, and his verses at Thag 16.9 give further details of his home life, his practice, and his past lives.
sn52.1:2.1: Despite Anuruddha’s love of solitude, his appearances in the discourses often feature his encounters with fellow monks, speaking to their warm and collegiate relationship.
sn52.1:3.1: Here Anuruddha extends the basic satipaṭṭhāna formula to include both internal/external and origination/vanishing.
